title: 发现“电子” (Electron)

video.title: J.J. 汤姆孙发现电子
video.title_en: Discovery Of Electron | How JJ Thomson discover electron

summary.text: J.J. 汤姆孙（J.J. Thomson）通过一系列巧妙的“阴极射线管”(Cathode Ray Tube) 实验，证明了“阴极射线”不是“波”（如赫兹 `hertz_waves_1887` 所认为的），而是一种“粒子流”。最重要的是，他通过测量这些粒子在“磁场”和“电场”中的“偏转”，成功地计算出了它们的“质荷比”(charge-to-mass ratio)。他发现，这些粒子（他称之为“微粒”corpuscles）的质量还不到“最轻”的“氢原子”的**千分之一**。他因此证明了，**原子不是不可分割的**（`dalton_atomic_theory_1803`），他发现了“第一个”亚原子粒子——“**电子**”(Electron)。
summary.text_en: J.J. Thomson, through a series of ingenious 'Cathode Ray Tube' experiments, proved that cathode rays were *not* waves (as Hertz, `hertz_waves_1887`, had thought) but a stream of *particles*. By measuring their 'deflection' in magnetic and electric fields, he calculated their 'charge-to-mass ratio'. He discovered these particles (which he called 'corpuscles') were over *1,000 times lighter* than the *lightest* atom, hydrogen. He had proved the atom was *not* indivisible (`dalton_atomic_theory_1803`) and had discovered the first subatomic particle: the '**Electron**'.
key_points: 证明了“原子是可分割的”
推翻了道尔顿 (`dalton_atomic_theory_1803`) 的“实心球”模型
使用了“阴极射线管”(Cathode Ray Tube)
计算出了电子的“质荷比”(charge-to-mass ratio)
提出了“葡萄干布丁模型”(Plum Pudding Model)

story.text: 在1890年代，物理学家们在争论“阴极射线”（在真空中通电时发出的神秘射线）到底是什么。德国物理学家（如赫兹 `hertz_waves_1887`）认为是“波”，而英国物理学家则认为是“粒子”。汤姆孙设计了一个决定性的实验。他用“电场”和“磁场”同时作用于阴极射线。他调整磁场，使磁力（`oersted_electromagnetism_1820`）“恰好”抵消了电场（`franklin_charge_1747`）的偏转，使射线“径直”射中屏幕。通过这个“平衡”的数学计算，他得以求出粒子的“质荷比”。当他发现这个粒子的“质量”比“氢原子”小1000多倍时，他意识到自己发现了一种“全新的”东西，一个“原子”的“组成部分”。为了解释这一点，他提出了“葡萄干布丁模型”：原子是一个“带正电的布丁”，里面嵌着“带负电的电子”（葡萄干）。
story.text_en: In the 1890s, physicists debated what 'cathode rays' were. German physicists (like Hertz, `hertz_waves_1887`) thought 'waves'; British physicists thought 'particles'. J.J. Thomson designed the definitive experiment. He applied *both* an electric field and a magnetic field at the same time. He 'balanced' them perfectly, so the magnetic force (`oersted_electromagnetism_1820`) *exactly* cancelled the electric force (`franklin_charge_1747`), making the beam hit 'straight on'. This 'balancing act' allowed him to *calculate* the particle's 'charge-to-mass ratio'. When he found the mass was *1000x lighter* than a *hydrogen atom*, he knew he had found something *new*—a 'piece' of an atom. To explain this, he proposed the 'Plum Pudding Model': a 'pudding' of positive charge, with tiny, negative 'plum' electrons embedded inside.

fun_facts.text: 汤姆孙因“发现电子”（一个“粒子”）获得了1906年的诺贝尔物理学奖。讽刺的是，他的“儿子”乔治·佩吉特·汤姆孙（George Paget Thomson）在1937年也获得了诺贝尔奖，因为他“证明了电子是一种波”（波粒二象性）。
fun_facts.text_en: J.J. Thomson won the 1906 Nobel Prize for discovering the electron (a *particle*). Ironically, his son, George Paget Thomson, won the Nobel Prize in 1937 for proving the electron is a *wave* (wave-particle duality).

fun_facts.text: 汤姆孙的实验室（卡文迪许实验室）是“诺贝尔奖工厂”。在他的领导下，他的“学生”和“同事”中，有八位最终获得了诺贝尔奖（包括卢瑟福 `rutherford_nucleus_1911`）。
fun_facts.text_en: Thomson's lab (the Cavendish) was a 'Nobel Prize factory'. *Eight* of his research assistants and colleagues (including Rutherford, `rutherford_nucleus_1911`) went on to win Nobel Prizes after working under him.

simple_explanation.text:
在1897年之前，所有人都认为“原子”（`dalton_atomic_theory_1803`）是“不可分割”的“最小积木”。
汤姆孙就像是第一个“敲开”这块“乐高积木”的人。他用“电”和“磁”在一个“真空管”（旧电视机显像管）里“玩弄”一种神秘的“阴极射线”。
他发现，这些“射线”是由一种“微小的、带负电的“碎屑””组成的。当他“称量”这些“碎屑”时，他发现它们比“最小的积木”（氢原子）还要“轻”1000多倍！
他证明了“原子”不是“实心”的，而是由“更小”的“零件”组成的。他发现了“电子”。
simple_explanation.text_en:
Before 1897, everyone thought 'atoms' (`dalton_atomic_theory_1803`) were the 'smallest possible thing'—like an indivisible LEGO brick.
J.J. Thomson was the first person to *smash the brick*. He 'zapped' a vacuum tube (an old TV tube) and played with the 'cathode rays' inside using magnets and electricity.
He discovered these 'rays' were made of *tiny, negative 'chips'*. When he 'weighed' these 'chips', he found they were *1,000 times lighter* than the *smallest known atom* (Hydrogen)!
He had proved the 'atom' was *not* solid, but was made of *even smaller parts*. He had discovered the 'electron'.

applications.title: 原子模型 (Atomic Model)
applications.text: 汤姆孙的“葡萄干布丁模型”（电子嵌在正电荷“凝胶”中）是第一个“有结构”的原子模型，取代了道尔顿的“实心球”模型。
applications.text_en: Thomson's 'Plum Pudding Model' (electrons embedded in a positive 'goo') was the *first* structured model of the atom, replacing Dalton's 'solid ball'.

applications.title: 阴极射线管 (CRT)
applications.text: 他证明了阴极射线（电子束）可以被“电场”和“磁场”精确“操纵”。这成为了所有“旧式电视机”和“电脑显示器”的工作原理。
applications.text_en: He proved that cathode rays (beams of electrons) could be *steered* by electric and magnetic fields. This is the principle that made all 'old' televisions and computer monitors work.

applications.title: 质谱仪 (Mass Spectrometer)
applications.text: 汤姆孙（和阿斯顿）后来改进了他的“质荷比”设备，发明了“质谱仪”，这是一种能“称量”不同原子的“同位素”的“天平”。
applications.text_en: Thomson (and Aston) later refined his 'm/e' apparatus into the 'Mass Spectrometer', a 'scale' that can 'weigh' different 'isotopes' of an atom.

impact.text: “电子”的发现，是“经典物理学”的终结，也是“量子革命”（`planck_quantum_1900`）的开端。它证明了“原子”不是“最终的”现实，而是由“更小”的、神秘的“亚原子粒子”构成的。它开创了“粒子物理学”，并提出了一个全新的问题：“如果电子是负的，那么原子的‘正电荷’藏在哪里？” 这个问题最终由他的学生卢瑟福（`rutherford_nucleus_1911`）在1911年解答。
impact.text_en: The discovery of the 'electron' was the *end* of classical physics and the *beginning* of the quantum revolution (`planck_quantum_1900`). It proved the 'atom' was *not* the fundamental reality, but was a *composite* object made of *smaller, stranger* 'subatomic particles'. It opened the field of 'particle physics' and posed the *next great question*: 'If the electrons are negative, where is the *positive* charge hiding?' His student, Rutherford (`rutherford_nucleus_1911`), would answer that in 1911.

influenced_by.contribution: 赫兹（其“阴极射线”实验（错误地）得出“射线是波”的结论，是汤姆孙试图“反驳”的）
influenced_by.contribution_en: Heinrich Hertz (his experiments on cathode rays, which *incorrectly* concluded they were waves, were what Thomson 'disproved')

influenced_by.contribution: 麦克斯韦（其“电磁理论”是汤姆孙计算“质荷比”的数学基础）
influenced_by.contribution_en: Maxwell (his 'electromagnetic theory' provided the mathematical basis for Thomson's e/m calculations)

influenced.contribution: 卢瑟福（他的学生，其“金箔实验”就是为了“验证”（并最终“推翻”）汤姆孙的“葡萄干布丁模型”）
influenced.contribution_en: Ernest Rutherford (his student, whose 'gold foil experiment' was designed to *test* (and *disproved*) Thomson's 'plum pudding model')

influenced.contribution: 爱因斯坦（其“光电效应”理论，解释了“电子”是如何从金属中被“光子”释放出来的）
influenced.contribution_en: Einstein (his 'photoelectric effect' theory explained *how* Thomson's 'electrons' were liberated from metal by 'photons')

influenced.contribution: 尼尔斯·玻尔（其“原子模型”就是试图解释汤姆孙发现的“电子”是如何“绕着”卢瑟福发现的“原子核”转动的）
influenced.contribution_en: Niels Bohr (his 'atomic model' was the attempt to explain how Thomson's 'electrons' orbit Rutherford's 'nucleus')

influence_chain.legacy_text: J.J. 汤姆孙“分裂”了（道尔顿的）原子，发现了“电子”，并提出了第一个（尽管是错误的）“原子模型”（葡萄干布丁）。
influence_chain.legacy_text_en: J.J. Thomson 'split' the (Dalton's) atom, discovered the 'electron', and proposed the *first* (though incorrect) 'model' of its structure: the 'plum pudding'.

related_concepts: 葡萄干布丁模型 (Plum Pudding Model)

quiz.question: J.J. 汤姆孙（J.J. Thomson）1897年的实验，如何证明了“原子”（`dalton_atomic_theory_1803`）不是“不可分割的”？
quiz.question_en: How did J.J. Thomson's 1897 experiment prove the 'atom' (`dalton_atomic_theory_1803`) was *not* indivisible?
options: 他发现了一种“粒子”（电子），其“质量”比“最小的”氢原子“小1000多倍”
他用化学方法合成了尿素
options_en: He discovered a particle (the 'electron') that was *over 1000 times lighter* than the *smallest* atom (Hydrogen)
He synthesized urea in a lab
quiz.explanation: 道尔顿（Dalton）的理论认为“原子”是“最小的”基本粒子。汤姆孙通过计算“质荷比”，证明了存在一种“更小”的粒子（他称之为“微粒”，我们称之为“电子”），它必定是从“原子”内部“剥离”出来的。
quiz.explanation_en: Dalton's theory held that the 'atom' was the smallest, fundamental particle. Thomson's calculation of the charge-to-mass ratio proved the existence of a *much smaller* particle (the 'corpuscle', or 'electron') that must have been 'chipped off' from *inside* the atom.
